The caller is only told whether the request was accepted. It is
not blocked until the Run Target is reached.
A pending Run Target is only picked up while the graph is in
kSuccess or kUndefinedState, so a cancelled transition is first
allowed to settle - see Transition Cancellation / Preemption.
set up a transition to the Run Target
The transition works in two phases:
1. Stopping phase: every component that is running and is not
needed by the target has to be stopped. This includes components left
running by an aborted transition before.
2. Starting phase: every component that is deactivated but is needed
by the target has to be activated.
[while the transition reports components that are ready to be started/stopped]
a component is ready to be activated/stopped
[the component is a Run Target node]
Run Target nodes are virtual and have no process, so
they finish immediately and can make further components
ready within the same dispatch loop.
activation or deactivation of the component

Only components without unfinished predecessors are dispatched;
the rest follow as their predecessors report back. Several
components are therefore in flight at the same time.
The graph moves to kAborting and the stop token is
requested: components that have not been taken by a
worker report as skipped, components in flight finish
their current step - see Transition Cancellation /

Starting phase: the components of the target subgraph
that are not active yet, starting with those that have
no dependencies left to wait for.

The graph moves to kSuccess: the requested Run Target
An aborted transition ends differently: once the last component
in flight has reported back, the graph moves to kUndefinedState
and the main loop starts a transition to the fallback Run Target
- see Process Termination and Supervision Failure.
The graph never waits for a component. It dispatches what is ready, returns to
the main loop, and advances the transition whenever a result arrives.
